Information security, including SCADA access control, is outside the scope of this document and shall be addressed by OES IT representative. 14 CORROSION CONTROL AND AC MITIGATION 14.1 CORROSION CONTROL Corrosion control will be provided per 49 CFR Part 195, Subpart H –Corrosion Control and ASME B31.4, and Project specifications. An internal corrosion monitoring and mitigation plan will be developed according to fluid characteristics. The pipeline system will be cathodically protected with an impressed current system. The cathodic protection (CP) design efforts for the pipeline will include field measurements of soil resistivity, Page 18 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 establishing electric isolation locations, and establishing ground bed/well and rectifier locations among other items. Electric isolation methods will be designed as required at each transition from buried to above grade piping. Isolation flange kits are to be located on barrel side of the first valve and on the station side of the by‐ pass valve for each trap. Test leads shall be installed on all foreign pipeline crossings, subject to approval by the operator of the foreign pipeline. Test leads shall also be considered for installation on both sides of public access roads, railroads, rivers, or other major waterway crossings greater than 100 feet wide, at accessible fence lines, and in enough quantity to accurately characterize the external corrosion protection system. The CP system will be installed and energized per 49 CFR 195 after the Pipeline is in service. 14.2 AC MITIGATION Any co‐locations with high‐voltage power lines will be evaluated to determine if there is a need for an AC mitigation system. Coupon test leads shall be placed at segments collocating with high‐voltage AC powerline to monitoring potential AC induced corrosion. 15 PIPELINE MARKERS Line markers shall be installed in accordance with US Code of Federal Regulations, Title 49 Part 195.410 and OES Project standards. A cathodic protection test station marker may also serve as a pipeline marker. Line markers shall be installed such that the location of the pipeline may be determined within the line of sight at any point on the pipeline right of way. When specified, buried warning ribbons are to be installed over each pipeline to mark the pipeline and alert any digging operations to the presence of the pipeline. 16 APPENDICES 16.1 APPENDIX A – CODES, REGULATIONS, STANDARDS & SPECIFICATIONS APPENDIX A APPLICABLE CODES, REGULATIONS, STANDARDS and SPECIFICATIONS Federal, State and Local Regulations Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Title 49 CFR Part 195 – Transportation of Hazardous Liquid by Pipelines Title 29 CFR Part 1910 and 1026 – OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Act) Rules and Regulations Industry Standards American Welding Society B.3.1 American Welding Society AWS A5.1 – Specification for Carbon Steel Electrodes for Shielded Metal Arc Welding AWS D1-10 – Structural Welding Code – Steel American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Page 19 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 ASME B 16.5 – Pipe
